turns.q:
Your response was: "Looked at it. Price section didn't work. Too many numbers at too many sizes. Couldn't spot the total without reading every label."

We want to understand what you meant by "couldn't spot the total without reading every label", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The visual hierarchy was confusing because the price for the "Wireless Mouse" ($39.99) is displayed in a much larger, bolder font than the final "Total" amount.
B) The layout lacked clear grouping or separation between the individual item prices and the summary section (Subtotal/Shipping), making it hard to distinguish which numbers were line items versus the final cost.
C) The label "Total" was visually competing with the other text in that section, failing to stand out as the primary anchor for the final price.
D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.

Looking at the "Order Summary" box, which specific visual element—like the thin line above "Subtotal" or the spacing between items—do you feel fails to clearly separate the individual product costs from the final totals?
turns.a: Sizes all over the place. Nothing obviously the most important one.

turns.q: If you were to pick just one number in that summary area to be visually dominant, which specific label—Subtotal, Shipping, or Total—would you enlarge and bold to make it stand out?
turns.a: Same. Had to read every label. Nothing stood out as the one.

turns.q: If a developer built this layout exactly as shown, how would that play out for someone encountering it for the first time?
turns.a: Nearly moved on without confirming the total. Too many sizes at similar weights — couldn't tell which was the main one. Stopped and read each label to confirm.

turns.q: If the layout were adjusted so that "Total" was clearly the dominant number, would that resolve your concern, or is there something deeper about how these sections are grouped that would still bother you?
turns.a: Total needs to be the largest number in the section — obviously so. Line items all the same size, clearly smaller. Secondary text smaller still. That's a typographic scale. Right now there are five sizes in that section. There should be three.
